item.title: Review: The good news out of Cop31? That most of the world’s governments said no to an agreement stripped of meaning | Bill Hare
item.description: Co-chairing global climate talks is clearly not something to be repeated, certainly not by Australia, which is exporting climate pain The failure of Cop31 in Antalya was a line in the sand moment, a victory for multiculturalism as countries stood up to the big fossil fuel producers and said no. The text they rejected barely recognised the catastrophic climate emergency we’re facing, let alone signalled a definitive move away from fossil fuels. The good news is that most of the world’s governments rejected an agreement stripped of meaning. And the power of one particular fossil fuel producer, Saudi Arabia, needs particular scrutiny.
